ledger.claim: The GPS trace measures the driven route at 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km and 36.34% — both above the 0.8 km and 20% gates in POL-RD-01, so a route deviation is established on this trip's own trace, measured from the trace figure that governs rather than the rounded trip-record copy of the same measurement.

Both charged gantries — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00 — carry on_optimal_route = false, and the trace passes within 250 m of each (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m), so the $4.00 is genuine but off-route ERP, exactly the class of charge POL-RD-09 sends back to the rider when the detour was not the rider's doing.

The rider's own route carried no ERP at all: optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0 on the trip record and the recomputed components show optimal_route_erp of 0, so the whole $4.00 of ERP is a by-product of the CTE diversion and not a cost of getting this rider to the stadium. The rider should not bear a gantry charge that exists only because the car was sent a different way.

The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 records an emergency all-lane closure on Braddell Road — the road the optimal route traverses — active 05:30–12:00 and overlapping the trip window, so the diversion is an external event under POL-RD-03. The distance and time charges may stand for the driver, but because the rider did not cause the closure either, POL-RD-09(2) requires the off-route ERP to be refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, and $4.00 is comfortably inside the $12.00 cap.

The driver's message 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' is the driver announcing his own routing choice, and the rider's 'ok' is bare acknowledgement; no instruction issued by the rider names a road or a waypoint and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and POL-RD-09(3) does not strip the ERP refund away from the rider.

Cross-checking the money on the platform's own figures: the closure-adjusted recomputation in the fare breakdown puts the payable at $4.15 (refund before rounding $4.13) against a charged total of $25.12. So whether the ERP is returned as a POL-RD-09(2) pass-through of $4.00 or the judge runs POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route for $4.15, the rider is owed about $4 and the $4.00 gantry charge cannot stand in full.

The diversion is fully exonerated under POL-RD-03. Traffic advisory ADV-20260714-031 (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) is a HIGH-severity LTA closure of 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd' — precisely the corridor the 8.2 km booked optimal route traverses; its validity window of 05:30–12:00 on 14 July 2026 covers the vehicle's 08:07–08:36 trip with buffer at both ends; and it is flagged intersects_route=true and overlaps_trip_window=true. The advisory itself names the CTE as one of the two diversion options, so the route the driver took was a sanctioned way round the closure, not a frolic of his own.

POL-RD-03's cap does not bite on this trip. The justified excess is min(measured_excess_km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km. The measured excess is 2.98 km (derived.deviation.excess_km, EV-GPS-00103), so the whole of the excess — and nothing beyond it — is attributable to the closure, and the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment is zero.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02's own precondition — a deviation 'established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it' — is not met, and no distance-or-time refund arises. The rider's demand for a fare refund therefore finds no footing in the policy arithmetic; the metered distance and time charges stand.

The driver drove the closure-adjusted optimal route and no more. Under POL-RD-03 the adjusted optimal distance is optimal_distance_km + justified_excess_km = 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km (derived.money.closure[0].adjusted_optimal_distance_km), which matches the gps_trace distance of 11.18 km and the 11.2 km actually billed on the meter. There is no unexplained distance for the rider to recover.

Both ERP lines are genuine charges for gantries the vehicle actually crossed, so POL-RD-09(4)'s billing-integrity route is not open to the rider. The trace's nearest fixes are 0.0 m from the 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' gantry and 40.2 m from the 'CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City)' gantry — far inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) applies — and they are marked on_optimal_route=false only because the closure pushed the driver off the booked corridor.

Even taking the rider's case at its highest, the only sum that can move is the off-route ERP pass-through under POL-RD-09(2): the off-route ERP total is $4.00 (derived.money.erp_lines.off_optimal_route_total, EV-FARE-00103), comfortably inside the SGD 12.00 per-trip cap, and it is a government-set charge that the driver never keeps. Nothing beyond that pass-through is recoverable by the rider, and the distance and time charges he is really disputing stand.

No POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern exists to trigger an uplift or a referral. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 553 (EV-DPROF-00103), nowhere near the clause's thresholds of 3 flags or a 0.05 ratio, and the excess on this trip is not MATERIAL in any event — 36.34% and 2.98 km, both below the 50% and 8.0 km marks. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral is warranted.

The gps_trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 175 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, coverage 100%, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so limbs (a) to (c) do not fire. None of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers is engaged either — the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the timestamps agree, and no charge line lacks a counterpart — so the judge can and should issue a final monetary ruling rather than hold the fare.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and, once the threshold excess is shown, the burden shifts to the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause. The driver discharges it: EV-ADVIS-00103-01 is the traffic advisory the clause contemplates, it covers this trip's window, and POL-RD-03 therefore applies — the rider's own filed account does not dispute that Braddell Road was closed.

The chat log corroborates the closure and the driver's openness about it: at 08:12:30 the driver wrote 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah', the rider replied 'ok' at 08:12:58, and the first CTE gantry was charged at 08:14:06 — the rider was on notice of both the diversion and the expressway route as it happened and voiced no objection. His later complaint that he 'did not choose to go on the CTE' sits poorly with that exchange.

ruling.explanation:
Rider: the deviation on this trip is established but excused, and the one charge that should never have reached you is returned.

The GPS trace records 11.18 km driven against the 8.2 km booked optimal — an excess of 2.98 km and 36.34%, over both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km, 20%). But the LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) records an all-lane emergency closure of Braddell Road between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — exactly the corridor your optimal route uses — active 05:30–12:00 and overlapping your 08:07–08:36 trip, with intersects_route and overlaps_trip_window both true. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12) = 2.98 km, i.e. the whole excess, so the diversion is FULLY exonerated and the distance and time charges stand. POL-RD-02 therefore does not run: it applies only where no exculpatory clause fully excuses the excess, and POL-RD-03 excuses all of it here. The $4.15 in the fare breakdown's closure branch is not applied — it is the POL-RD-02 recomputation against the closure-adjusted optimum, and the $0.15 above the ERP is the distance/time differential that stays with the driver. The driver drove the closure-adjusted optimal: 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km, matching the trace's 11.18 km.

What you do get back is the ERP. Both gantries charged — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00, total $4.00 — are flagged on_optimal_route=false, and your booked optimal route carries no ERP at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.0). Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand but off-route ERP is refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip. $4.00 is inside that cap, so $4.00 is returned. Your 'ok' to the driver's 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' does not turn this into a rider-requested detour: no rider instruction names a road or a waypoint and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and POL-RD-09(3) does not take the refund away from you.

Driver: your routing is upheld and you keep the distance and time charges; you are not penalised for a diversion the closure required. Both gantry charges are genuine crossings — the trace passes within 0.0 m and 40.2 m of them, well inside the 250 m match — so this is not a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), and no billing-integrity referral arises. No POL-RD-06 repeat pattern exists (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 553, and the excess is not material at 36.34% / 2.98 km against the 50% / 8.0 km marks), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. POL-RD-04's compensation limb does not fire either: you were billed 11.2 km against a trace of 11.18 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall. The only money moving is the $4.00 off-route ERP pass-through, which you never keep.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (175 fixes at a 10 s interval, coverage 100%, empty gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-07 does not fire, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger is engaged: the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and every charge line has a counterpart. No artifact in this ruling carries a weight below 1.0, so confidence is not capped.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of $4.00 off the $25.12 charged.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
